title: Does Jensen Huang seriously want his job back?
transcript:
Speaker 0: Today's biggest news from The Australian. I'm Claire Harvey with The Front's afternoon headlines.
Speaker 0: Well, this would be an all time comeback story. Jensen Huang, the fallen CEO founder of NVIDIA,
Speaker 0: reportedly wants to come back, and he has Donald Trump behind him. Last week, Huang revealed he'd had an extramarital
Speaker 0: affair and apologized for putting his family and the business through his personal dramas. The other woman turned out to be someone American authorities suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Speaker 0: Then another alleged affair emerged, and on Thursday, Jensen Huang resigned from NVIDIA.
Speaker 0: Now there are reports the White House, Elon Musk, and other tech execs are backing Huang's return.
Speaker 0: Although US treasury secretary Scott Besson says NVIDIA should hire an outsider to reset the company that's at the center of the global AI revolution.
Speaker 0: The NVIDIA story has a national security twist not just because of the alleged honey trap operation by Chinese spy agencies,
Speaker 0: but because it's now suspected of funneling its high powered AI chips to Chinese interests in contravention of US export restrictions.
Speaker 0: Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is accusing Elon Musk's SpaceX of helping Russia by limiting Ukraine's access to the Star Shield satellite system.
Speaker 0: Star Shield is the military grade equivalent of Musk's Starlink satellite Internet business for domestic and business users.
Speaker 0: Ukraine says Star Shield satellite system has been deliberately slowed,
Speaker 0: making it more difficult to intercept Russian jet powered drones.
Speaker 0: SpaceX denies it's made any new changes.
Speaker 0: The future of gas is in doubt, and the Albanese government's got itself into conflict with the industry, which says the plan to reserve gas for domestic use could actually have the opposite effect. Modeling commissioned by energy producers warns the system could disrupt the East Coast market, undermine competition,
Speaker 0: and push up prices for households and businesses.
Speaker 0: Check out those stories live right now at theaustralian.com.au,
Speaker 0: and come back to the front first thing in the morning for our look at the billionaires circling
Speaker 0: DJs
Speaker 0: and what they would do to Australia's beloved retail brand. That's right here Tuesday morning.
themes: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's resignation following affairs and potential Chinese spy involvement, with Trump and tech executives backing his return despite national security concerns
Ukraine accuses SpaceX of limiting Star Shield satellite access to hinder drone interception capabilities against Russia
Australian government's gas reservation policy creates industry conflict over potential market disruption and household price increases
